title: Adaptive sequence census & pad-digestor for microbatch slimming
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Reduce wasted token padding and improve token/latency efficiency for mixed-length workloads by introducing a lightweight in-flight sequence-length census and a "pad-digestor" component that trims/elides unnecessary padding prior to kernel selection and decode scheduling. The feature should be safe for KV-cached prefill scenarios and compatible with existing rollout/fallback policies.

Background: Current runtime batching still incurs significant pad waste for highly skewed seq-length distributions (chat + short prompts). We observed a baseline pad ratio of ~38% across several customer workloads, translating to ~22% token-cost overhead and 8-12% median latency inflation on high-utilization hosts. Existing bucketizers rely on coarse offline histograms or per-request heuristics and do not coordinate with kernel variant selection or prefill-aware scheduling.

Approach:
- Sequence census: maintain a low-overhead sliding-window histogram of recent sequence lengths per runtime shard (exponential decay). This is used to compute transient bucket boundaries and an 'active-trim-threshold' per shard.
- Pad-digestor: at microbatch formation time, apply safe trim/elision rules to trailing padding and optional tail tokens (when model/usage semantics permit). Trimming operates in two modes: conservative (drop only explicit pad tokens) and aggressive (elide predictable soft padding based on prefix affinity).
- Kernel hinting: expose resulting shaped microbatch profiles to the kernel selection layer so it can pick the kernel variant optimized for the new (reduced-padding) shapes (e.g., smaller attention tiling / different shared-memory layout).
- Prefill/decode scheduling tie-in: prioritize short sequences for burst-prefill packing while ensuring low-impact reordering (maintain per-request arrival monotonicity for KV cache correctness). Add a prefill guard that forces full-length prefill for requests with complex cache dependencies.

Targets:
- Reduce pad ratio by >=60% on mixed-length workloads.
- Improve token-level cost by >=10% on targeted customers.
- No regression in 95th percentile latency (<= +2% vs baseline).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Over-aggressive trimming could change model outputs for padding-sensitive prompts. Mitigation: tag requests with 'sensitive-pad' at SDK/API and fall back to conservative mode.
- Risk: Additional CPU/heap cost for census maintenance. Mitigation: use bounded fixed-size histograms and amortize updates into tracer threads; offload heavy ops to worker CPUs.
- Risk: Kernel selection complexity increases. Mitigation: limit kernel variants exposed and provide safe defaults; add telemetry to monitor kernel-switch churn.
acceptance_criteria: Automated perf harness shows >=60% pad reduction on synthetic mixed-length trace compared to current bucketing baseline
End-to-end canary at 5% of runtime capacity without functional regressions in SDK integration tests
Kernel selector uses pad-digestor hints and selects a different kernel variant in >=30% of shaped batches where latency improvement expected
No customer-facing errors introduced; error rate change <= 0.1% during canary
Dashboard with per-shard pad ratio, kernel-variant distribution, and tail-latency deltas is available in Console
implementation_notes: Sequence census stored as 128-bin exponential histogram per shard; update path is lock-free with single-writer/backoff
Pad-digestor API: ShapeProfile {avg_len, p90_len, pad_ratio_est}; return a small token-remap table for kernel to apply without copying the full tensor
Kernel selection hook to accept ShapeProfile and return kernel_id + tuning_params; fall back to current behavior if kernel latency model confidence < 0.7
Prefill scheduler changes: introduce reorder window (10ms) to opportunistically group short sequences; requests flagged 'kv_strict' bypass reorder
Telemetry: add new metrics (pad_ratio_per_shard, trimmed_tokens, kernel_switch_rate, trimmed_by_mode) with percentiles
test_plan: Unit tests for census histogram updates, boundary conditions, and rollover behavior
Microbench harness: replay representative customer traces (chat, assistant, batch inference) and measure pad ratio and per-token throughput
A/B canary: 5% -> 25% -> 100% rollout with automated smoke checks, regression thresholds for latency and error rates
Fuzzing: generate adversarial sequences (all-short, all-long, heavy-tail) to verify no correctness loss
Model-output QA: run model-output diff checks on curated prompt-set flagged as padding-sensitive
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): unit + integration tests, local perf runs (target runtime team validation)
Phase 2 (canary): enable on small subset of shards (5%), run for 48h, collect pad/latency/kernel metrics
Phase 3 (ramp): increase to 25% and 60% with manual checkpoints; rollback if error rate or 95th-latency exceed thresholds
Phase 4 (full): enable by default with opt-out via per-tenant flags for customers requiring full-length prefill
